title: Effective nonlinear electromagnetism and semiclassical consistency

items.title: Continuous compact-support integration for the constitutive action
items.design_state: Step 2 owner-authorized same-pair local proof; source release recorded, ordinary native gates pending.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff second-countable oriented four-manifold without boundary. A continuous real top form is a continuous section of $\Lambda^4T^*M$: in every smooth coordinate chart it has the form $f(x)\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4$ with continuous real coefficient $f$, and the coefficients transform by the determinant of the coordinate-transition derivative. Its support is the closure in $M$ of its nonzero locus. Write $C_c^0(\Lambda^4T^*M)$ for these forms with compact support.

For $\omega\in C_c^0(\Lambda^4T^*M)$, put $K=\operatorname{supp}\omega$. If $K=\varnothing$, define its integral to be zero. Otherwise choose finitely many positively oriented charts $(U_i,\phi_i)$ and smooth functions $\chi_i:M\to[0,1]$ with compact support contained in $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Write
$$
(\phi_i^{-1})^*(\chi_i\omega)=f_i\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4
$$
on $\phi_i(U_i)$ and extend $f_i$ by zero to $\mathbb R^4$, obtaining $\widetilde f_i$. Define
$$
\mathcal I_M(\omega):=\sum_i\int_{\mathbb R^4}\widetilde f_i(x)\,dx,
$$
where each Euclidean integral is the Riemann integral over any closed nondegenerate rectangle whose interior contains its support. Such finite cutoffs exist, each zero extension is continuous and compactly supported, and the value is independent of the chosen charts, cutoffs and bounding rectangles. This is a linear functional on $C_c^0(\Lambda^4T^*M)$. For fixed cutoffs and bounding rectangles $Q_i$, it satisfies $|\mathcal I_M(\omega)|\le\sum_i\operatorname{vol}(Q_i)\sup_{Q_i}|\widetilde f_i|$; thus uniform convergence of these finitely many zero-extended coefficients implies convergence of their integrals. If an open set $V\subseteq M$ contains $K$, then $\mathcal I_V(\omega|_V)=\mathcal I_M(\omega)$, with the restricted orientation. On smooth compactly supported top forms it equals the previously defined smooth manifold integral.

Countable Choice is retained to match that smooth integral's standing convention. The finite-cover construction and comparison for continuous coefficients below require no further choice principle, and do not assume the full Axiom of Choice.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, Chapter 16, chart-partition integration formula
references.locator: The existing pinned smooth integration definitions cite pp. 404–406. Their formula is extended to continuous coefficients by the local proof below; no new external full-text reading is claimed.

items.title: Nonlinear electromagnetic constitutive model with a $C^2$ Lagrangian
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, independent orientation $o$, and the torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ selected by $g$. Fix a smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle sector and a smooth connection $\mathcal A$ in that sector. In the inherited physical-curvature normalization, its curvature is a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $dF=0$. On a supplied countable trivializing cover $(U_i)$, write its compatible local physical-potential representatives as $A_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, so $F|_{U_i}=dA_i$ and, in the normalization of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]], $A_i=\kappa_0 a_i$ with $A_j-A_i=\kappa_0\lambda(g_{ij})$ on overlaps. No global potential is required.

A permitted variation is specified by a smooth compactly supported global real one-form $a\in\Omega^1(M)$, with the same component units as each $A_i$ if units are attached. For a dimensionless parameter $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, define $A_{i,\epsilon}:=A_i+\epsilon a|_{U_i}$. Because $a$ is global, these local representatives retain the same transition functions and define a smooth connection $\mathcal A_\epsilon$ in the same bundle sector. Equivalently, the normalized local representatives shift as $a_{i,\epsilon}=a_i+\epsilon\kappa_0^{-1}a|_{U_i}$. Thus $F_\epsilon|_{U_i}=dA_{i,\epsilon}=F|_{U_i}+\epsilon da$, so globally $F_\epsilon=F+\epsilon da$. The shorthand $\mathcal A_\epsilon=\mathcal A+\epsilon a$ denotes this affine shift of local physical-potential representatives; it does not assert direct addition of a base one-form to a principal-bundle connection one-form on its total space.

Raise indices with $g^{-1}$ and let $\star_g$ be the Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$. Define the scalar invariants
$$X:=-\frac14 F_{ab}F^{ab},\qquad Y:=-\frac14F_{ab}(\star_gF)^{ab}.$$
Let $L:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$, and write $L_X,L_Y$ for its first partial derivatives evaluated at $(X,Y)$. Define the contravariant antisymmetric tensor
$$H^{ab}:=L_XF^{ab}+L_Y(\star_gF)^{ab}.$$
The source-free local action density is $L(X,Y)\,\mathrm{vol}_g$. For a continuous compactly supported top form, use the finite chart-partition integral $\mathcal I_M$ of the continuous-integral definition linked below; it agrees with the usual manifold integral on smooth forms. This convention retains Countable Choice, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function, as inherited from the smooth integral. Its relative action difference under a compact variation is $\mathcal I_M([L(X(F_\epsilon),Y(F_\epsilon))-L(X(F),Y(F))]\,\mathrm{vol}_g)$; this difference has compact support even when the unvaried integral over $M$ is not finite. The connection is stationary when the derivative of this relative action at $\epsilon=0$ vanishes for every permitted $a$.

In the mathematical normalization, $L=X$ is the Maxwell quadratic term. If units are attached, the components of $F$ have a fixed unit $\mathfrak F$, $X,Y,L$ have unit $\mathfrak F^2$, and coefficients $\alpha,\beta$ in $L=X+\alpha X^2+\beta Y^2$ have unit $\mathfrak F^{-2}$, so $\alpha X$ and $\beta Y$ are dimensionless. This normalization is not an SI action prefactor. The coefficients are arbitrary parameters, not QED coefficients. This definition supplies no quantum origin, source coupling, characteristic-cone condition, hyperbolicity, causality, or solution-existence claim.

items.title: Constitutive field equation from compact variations
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use the fixed-metric, fixed-bundle-sector model of the nonlinear Lagrangian Definition: $F$ is its smooth closed real curvature two-form, $L\in C^2(\mathbb R^2)$, $X=-F_{ab}F^{ab}/4$, $Y=-F_{ab}(\star_gF)^{ab}/4$, and $H^{ab}=L_XF^{ab}+L_Y(\star_gF)^{ab}$. For dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, a permitted variation is a smooth compactly supported global real one-form $a$ added to each compatible local physical-potential representative, so $F_\epsilon=F+\epsilon da$; stationarity differentiates the relative $L(X,Y)\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ action difference. Its compactly supported density is integrated by the finite chart-partition rule for continuous top forms, agreeing with the usual integral on smooth forms; this convention retains $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. If the connection is stationary under every such variation and the source coupling is absent, then
$$\nabla_aH^{ab}=0,\qquad dF=0.$$
For $L=X+\alpha X^2+\beta Y^2$ this gives
$$H^{ab}=(1+2\alpha X)F^{ab}+2\beta Y(\star_gF)^{ab}.$$
Here $\alpha,\beta$ are arbitrary fixed real parameters with units inverse to those of $X,Y$ when units are attached. This is a conditional Euler–Lagrange deduction for the stated mathematical model; it does not assign QED coefficients or assert that a field solves the equations. The variation alone gives no hyperbolicity, causal-cone, uniqueness, or well-posedness result.

items.title: Conditional semiclassical Einstein–Maxwell source contract
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary. Equip it with a smooth nondegenerate Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth timelike vector field $N$ selecting a time orientation, and an independent orientation $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, metric-compatible connection selected by $g$, as in the oriented Lorentzian geometry convention recorded in the Definition references. For SI coordinate bookkeeping, use length coordinates with $x^0=ct$, where $c>0$ is the coordinate-conversion scale with unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; this assigns no measured value to $c$. Fix $\mu_0>0$ in the inherited SI convention. A smooth real two-form $F$ assigns to each $p\in M$ an alternating bilinear map $F_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$, with coefficients smooth in charts.

For a vector bundle $E\to M$ with projection $\pi_E$, write $\Gamma(E)$ for its smooth sections, namely smooth maps $s:M\to E$ such that $\pi_E\circ s=\operatorname{id}_M$. The bundle $\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*M$ is the subbundle of $T^*M\otimes T^*M$ whose fibers are symmetric bilinear forms. A unital complex $*$-algebra $\mathfrak A_{g,F}$ means an associative complex algebra with unit $1$ and an antilinear involution satisfying $(AB)^*=B^*A^*$ and $1^*=1$. A state on this algebra means a complex-linear functional $\omega$ such that $\omega(1)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathfrak A_{g,F}$. Choose a specified state class $\mathscr S_{g,F}$ of such states, with any additional regularity conditions stated as part of that choice.

A renormalization prescription $\mathcal R$ is a fixed item of input recording the subtraction rule, scale, and finite local counterterms used for the source assignments. A candidate assignment consists of maps
$$\omega\longmapsto T_{\mathcal R}[g,F,\omega]\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*M),\qquad \omega\longmapsto j_{\mathcal R}[g,F,\omega]\in\Gamma(TM),$$
for $\omega\in\mathscr S_{g,F}$, with smooth spacetime fields. In the inherited SI bookkeeping, $F$ has units $\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $j_{\mathcal R}$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $T_{\mathcal R}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$; these are formal units, not observations. The maps may depend nonlocally on the state.

Use the inverse metric $g^{-1}$ to raise indices, with $\nabla^a:=g^{ac}\nabla_c$.

The assignment is **contract-admissible** when, for every $\omega\in\mathscr S_{g,F}$,
$$\nabla_a j_{\mathcal R}^{a}=0,\qquad \nabla^a T_{\mathcal R,ab}=F_{bc}j_{\mathcal R}^{c}.$$
The current convention is the one in which the classical sourced Maxwell equation is $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ and the Maxwell stress divergence is $\nabla^aT^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}=-F_{bc}j^c$. The identities displayed in this definition are interface conditions; they do not construct $\mathfrak A_{g,F}$, $\mathscr S_{g,F}$, $\mathcal R$, or either source map, and they do not assert that any assignment is contract-admissible.

items.title: Necessary Ward consistency of coupled sources
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, $j\in\Gamma(TM)$, and $T_{\mathrm{ren}}\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*M)$ be smooth, with $\mu_0$ a positive real constant, $\kappa$ a nonzero real constant, and $\Lambda$ a constant real. Define
$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\frac12R g_{ab}.$$
Assume the mathematical field equations
$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T_{\mathrm{ren},ab}\right).$$
Then
$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla^aT_{\mathrm{ren},ab}=F_{bc}j^c.$$
These are necessary conditional consequences of the displayed equations and match the contract-admissibility identities of the source-contract Definition; in this item, “Ward consistency” means exactly these two divergence identities. In SI length-coordinate bookkeeping, $[F]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $[j]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_{\mathrm{ren}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and $[\kappa]=\mathrm{s^2\,kg^{-1}m^{-1}}$; the units are formal and no measured value is used. The result asserts no quantum-state construction, renormalized-source existence, or well-posed semiclassical evolution.

items.title: Small invariants do not alone control derivative corrections
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: In coordinates $(t,x,y,z)$ on Minkowski $\mathbb R^4$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dt\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, define $X_\epsilon=-(F_\epsilon)_{ab}(F_\epsilon)^{ab}/4$ and $Y_\epsilon=-(F_\epsilon)_{ab}(\star_\eta F_\epsilon)^{ab}/4$. The refuted assertion is: for every fixed finite $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$ and every family $(F_\epsilon)_{0<\epsilon<1}$ of smooth exact real two-forms on $\mathbb R^4$ (that is, $F_\epsilon=dA_\epsilon$ for a smooth real one-form $A_\epsilon$), if $\sup_{\mathbb R^4}(|\alpha X_\epsilon|+|\beta Y_\epsilon|)\to0$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, then there exist $C\ge0$ and $\epsilon_0\in(0,1)$ such that $\sup_{\mathbb R^4}|\partial_x(F_\epsilon)_{tx}|\le C$ for every $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$. The assertion says that small invariant corrections alone give a local uniform bound on this derivative scale.
